# Embedded Modules (generated by build.rs)

This repository uses a small `build.rs` helper to transform upstream crates and expose
them as modules in the final WASM build. The script copies selected `src/` trees
into `OUT_DIR` and generates `embedded_mods.rs`, which contains `pub mod` wrappers
that `include!` the transformed sources.

Why we do this
- Keep the WASM build small and self-contained.
- Apply small text transformations to upstream code so it compiles under the guest
  environment (e.g., `crate::` -> `crate::brush_core::`).
- Centralize the mapping list in one place (`build.rs`) so adding/removing crates
  is straightforward.

Where to look
- `build.rs` — the authoritative place to add or remove mappings. Edit the
  `mappings` array there.
- `OUT_DIR/embedded_mods.rs` — generated at build time. It contains doc comments
  that point to the original source path (useful for IDE hovers).

Maintenance checklist
- When adding a new upstream repository:
  1. Add an entry to the `mappings` array in `build.rs` (format: `("path/to/src", "dest-name")`).
  2. Run `cargo check` locally. The build script validates that the source path exists and will fail early if it doesn't.
  3. Inspect `target/*/out/embedded_mods.rs` to make sure the generated `pub mod` entry looks right.

IDE notes
- Rust Analyzer runs `build.rs` by default, so it will see `embedded_mods.rs` and
  index its contents. However, "Go to Definition" will point to the generated
  file under `target/.../out/`, not the original upstream source directory.
- The generated `embedded_mods.rs` contains `/// Source: <path>` comments to help
  readers and hover text.
- If you need IDE navigation to go to the original upstream sources, consider
  adding a `rust-project.json` or making the upstream crates separate workspace
  members (heavier approaches).

Troubleshooting
- Build script panics with `Expected mapped source path '...' to exist`:
  - Either fetch or checkout the required repo at the expected path, or adjust
    the `mappings` entry in `build.rs`.
- Generated modules not visible in the IDE:
  - Ensure your editor runs build scripts (Rust Analyzer setting: `rust-analyzer.cargo.runBuildScripts`).

Optional improvements (future work)
- Add a CI check that ensures `build.rs` mappings are valid and `cargo check`
  passes on CI.
- Embed the generator's git hash / timestamp in `embedded_mods.rs` for provenance.

---
